key_insight: OpenGEM26 provides a large, diverse molecular trajectory dataset that enables a graph neural network force field (GPTFF-mol) to learn accurate energies and forces for organic molecules, including sulfur- and chlorine-containing species.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical machine-learning potential for faster atomistic simulations, reducing reliance on costly DFT while preserving strong accuracy for conformational and reactive dynamics.
method: Built OpenGEM26 with 200,000 unique molecules and 4.4 million conformations from full optimization trajectories.
Computed data at ωB97X-D/Def2-SVP and Def2-TZVP with dispersion corrections for H/C/N/O/S/Cl molecules up to ten heavy atoms.
Trained GPTFF-mol on these trajectories to predict molecular energies and forces with a graph neural network.
evidence_signal: The model reaches 16 meV/molecule energy MAE (0.82 meV/atom) and outperforms ANI-2x on force prediction, while tests on butane rotation and keto-enol tautomerization show good barrier and dynamics fidelity.
watch_item: The dataset is limited to molecules with up to ten heavy atoms and the reported validation focuses on benchmark molecules, so broader transfer to larger or chemically more exotic systems remains to be verified.
paper_title: Graph Neural Network Force Fields (GPTFF-mol) for Organic Molecules from Optimization Trajectories (OpenGEM26)
